To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the recall advantage for trait-congruent over trait-incongruous behaviors found in previous studies is reduced when the target is expected to be a member of an ethnic group, and that (2) this reduction is not dependent on the ethnicity of the participant.
the combination of trait information and stereotype information reduced the standard advantage in memory for stereotype-incongruent behavior information.
the combination of stereotype and trait information can reduce the recall advantage for trait incongruent behaviors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the combined effects of stereotypes and traits.
the role of stereotypes in person memory.
the role of stereotypes in the encoding and recall of behavioral information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stereotype expectancies have the effect of reducing the recall of information that is inconsistent with the expectancy.
stereotype expectancies have an effect on the recall of trait-incongruencies.
the combination of trait expectancies with stereotype expectancies reduces the recall advantage for incongruent trait information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of trait expectancies and stereotypes results in more stereotypical memory.

stereotype expectancies have an impact on the organization and recall of information about individuals, even when no stereotype information is presented about the individual, and that the impact of stereotype expectancies is greater when stereotype information is provided about the target.
the combination of trait expectancies and stereotype expectancies results in the retrieval of more information than would occur with either expectancy type alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trait and stereotype information can combine to produce a memory advantage for expectancy-congruent information.
the combination of stereotype and trait information can reduce the recall of trait-incongruous behavior.
stereotype expectancies may have a more powerful influence than trait expectancies when the two types of expectancies are combined.
